Derya Yıldırım & Grup Şimşek with Thee Marloes
events.info: Derya Yıldırım & Grup Şimşek with Thee MarloesSould Out Presents: Derya Yıldırım & Grup Şimşek with Thee Marloes.Doors: 7:00pmShow: 8:00pmAges 21+.https://deryayildirimgrupsimsek.com/ https://www.instagram.com/theemarloes Derya Yıldırım is singing the song her grandmother used to sing an old Anatolian folk standard called Hop Bico, which roughly translates as Hop Around Bico. But the version Deryas grandmother sang was different shed put her own slant on it. And Deryas is different still brought into the 21st century with a slow psychedelic twist and her own hypnotic vocals. This is by design. Derya insists that if youre going to play an old folk song then you have to contribute something new, otherwise you might as well just put the old record on.Born in Hamburg, Germany to Turkish parents, she grew up influenced by her familys Anatolian background and the myriad of cultures in the city. Deryas musical roots started at home playing folk music with family members. Her father pushed her to learn various instruments, beginning with the bağlama, a seven stringed Turkish lute. Then she picked up the guitar, piano, and saxophone.

ZACCAI CURTIS - CUBOP LIVES
events.info: Zaccai Curtis - Cubop LivesSould Out Presents: Zaccai Curtis Cubop LivesDoors: 7:00pmShow: 8:00pmZaccai Curtis - Piano, Luques Curtis - Bass, Willie Martinez - Timbales, Camilo Molina -Congas, Reinaldo De Jesus - Congas, Jeremy Bosch - Flute2025 GRAMMY Award winner Zaccai Curtis is a multi-faceted pianist for whom every side of his work gleams. Equal parts performer, composer, educator, and producer, Curtis has won himself esteem in each area as he vibrantly showcases his mastery of both the Jazz and Afro-Caribbean Jazz lineages.As a musician who is so deeply steeped in the Jazz and Bebop tradition and so vivaciously immersed in the worlds of Afro-Cuban Jazz, Curtis found himself wanting to pay homage to the great musicians in whose steps he has trod who brought together the distinct fusion of these musical cultures. I wanted to make a period piece album that brought a new perspective to an older style one that wasnt covered the way I thought it could be, Curtis says. Cubop Lives! points out the earliest of jazz fusion and the combination of cultures that related to each other socially, politically and, of course, musically.Curtis brings along his Quartet, which expands upon the CUBOP era, with a mix of new compositions and classics from Dizzy Gillespie, Kenny Dorham to Machito. Exploring these classic Afro-Cuban jazz concepts this quartet brings a new sound through their arrangements and vision of where this music should go. This group features bassist Luques Curtis, timbaleroWillie Martinez, conguero Camilo Molina, bongosero Reinaldo De Jesus and flautist Jeremy Bosch.---JLR Seating Map Notes: For this show, you may reserve individual tables on the map pictured. events.info: Grab your boots (or anything thats comfy) and come get ready for Friends in Low Places with us! We're taking over The Showdown for a night of line dancing, prizes, karaoke, and plenty of '90s country. Whether you're already a regular on the dance floor or have absolutely no idea what you're doing, this night is for you. We'll kick things off with three beginner-friendly line dances taught by Friends in Low Places co-founder Cara Lindsay. No experience necessary---we'll break them down step-by-step so everyone can join in. Then, try your luck in our raffle featuring multiple prizes! Every admission comes with one raffle ticket, with additional tickets available for purchase throughout the night. Once we've learned our moves and handed out some prizes, we're ending the night the only way we know how: a big ol' country karaoke party. Come learn some moves, sing some songs, make some friends, and get warmed up for the next Friends in Low Places: '90s Country Night. No line dancing experience required. Just bring yourself, your friends, and maybe your boots."

With a collective resume that reads like a Whos Who of NW jazz, blues, and soul, this group has the talent and confidence to be completely spontaneous --from their blistering solos to their improvised arrangements and segues. No wonder theyve thrilled audiences wherever theyve played. Count among the bands fans jazz great Christian McBride, host of National Public Radios Jazz Night In America.
